generated.title: Myth or Fact: Can a Tsunami Hit San Francisco? #shorts
generated.description:
Can a tsunami really hit San Francisco?

FACT. Although rare, tsunamis can reach the city's coastline and parts of San Francisco Bay.

In 1964, a tsunami generated by the massive Alaska earthquake damaged boats and marina facilities in the Bay Area.

Discover how powerful undersea earthquakes generate tsunamis, why the San Andreas Fault behaves differently, and what California's official tsunami hazard maps tell us about coastal safety.

A tsunami doesn't have to look like a giant breaking wave to be dangerous. Strong currents and fast flooding can threaten beaches, marinas and low-lying waterfront areas.

Explore the official California tsunami hazard maps:
https://www.conservation.ca.gov/cgs/tsunami/maps/san-francisco

Official tsunami alerts:
https://www.tsunami.gov/

This educational video includes AI-generated illustrative reconstructions and schematic scientific visualizations. These are not authentic historical footage, documented tsunami imagery or predictions of future flooding.
